newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals sluggish and range-bound.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals sluggish and range-bound.

text.p: The precious metals markets were very quiet on Monday ahead of the New Year's holiday and prices were expected to remain mired in tiny ranges this week.
Gold was fixed at $369.60 an ounce, up slightly from $369.40 on Friday afternoon and a London close of $369.30/$369.80.
"It's very quiet, there's nothing interesting in bullion. We haven't traded all morning," a dealer said.
Prices had barely moved overnight in Asian trading, sticking to the $368-$370 range which has dominated the market over the past three weeks.
"I don't see gold moving out of range until people start fresh in the new year next week," the dealer added.
However, gold was poised to break out of this band, with price charts and sour market sentiment favouring the downside, some dealers and analysts said.
"We're still seeing (gold) at $365 and below eventually," one dealer said.
"Gold has been in a bear market and got oversold, but now indicators are no longer overstretched and yet prices have not gone up," a European bullion analyst noted.
In the immediate term, the comatose gold market continued to ignore the dollar's recent strength against the yen.
The dollar had surged to 45-month highs against the yen on Friday and was still holding firm in early European trading on Monday, although it has eased below Friday's peaks.
Silver, like gold, was virtually static in early trading. It was indicated two cents lower at $4.89/$4.91 an ounce.
A move above the psychological $5.00 level would be required to encourage buying, analysts said.
Platinum was up slightly at $370.00/$371.00 an ounce, a rise of $1.25.
